text:
INPUT:
Obsession: Repetitive thoughts about violently attacking my family with a kitchen knife.
Compulsion: Counting rituals and avoidance of the kitchen to prevent acting on violent urges.
Feared consequence: I will snap and brutally murder my wife and children, destroying my family and myself.
Script intensity: 9/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
Every day, I live in terror that I will lose control and slaughter my family. The thoughts are so vivid - grabbing the largest knife from the butcher block, creeping into my children's rooms as they sleep, and slashing their throats. I picture their blood spraying the walls as they gurgle and choke, their little eyes wide with confusion and fear. Then I'd move on to my wife, stabbing her again and again as she screams and tries to fight me off. Her desperate pleas for mercy would be futile against the savage rage consuming me. After it's done, I'd be left in a nightmarish scene straight out of a horror movie, my mind and soul shattered by what I've done. The police would come and I'd be arrested, my picture plastered all over the news as the monster who butchered his own family. I'd spend the rest of my days in a cage, tortured by guilt and the certainty that I deserve to die for my unspeakable crimes. This is the nightmare I face every moment of every day. The counting and avoidance give me no real safety, just a fragile illusion. Deep down, I know I'm one horrible moment away from destroying everything I love. If I do lose control and murder them, I'll have to find a way to keep breathing, to face the consequences of my actions. Because the alternative is giving in to the fear and letting it consume me. I have to accept that I could be a killer to have any chance at a life worth living.

INPUT:
Obsession: Having repetitive thoughts about harming loved ones.
Compulsion: Mental compulsions aiming at neutralizing feared consequences that individual will not cause harm to loved ones.
Feared consequence: Individual will cause harm to the loved ones, and live life as a terrible person.
Script intensity: 7/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
There is no way for me to truly protect my wife and son from myself. I just have to live with the possibility that, just like everyone else, I could lose control and kill both of them tonight. If I do lose control, I might get my sheath knife and stab my little son in his sleep and then go to my wife and stab her before she has a chance to defend herself. Living with myself afterward would be so hardI dont know how I would be able to take it. Going through a trial, knowing I had done the most horrible thing I could think of, and then languishing in a prison with nothing to do but be tortured by what I had done. But this is the possibility I have to accept to get better. If I lose control and stab them to death, then Ill have to cope with it. For all my ritualizing, I never feel 100 percent safe. The rituals never really prove that I wont be responsible for choking the life out of my son.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts that I may secretly want to cheat on my partner, even though I have no desire to do so.
Compulsion: Repeatedly seeking reassurance from my partner that our relationship is secure, or mentally reviewing past interactions with others to 'prove' my loyalty.
Feared consequence: I will inevitably act on my intrusive thoughts, betraying my partner in the most devastating way possible and destroying our relationship.
Script intensity: 4/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I find myself noticing an attractive person at the coffee shop. The thought crosses my mind that perhaps I would enjoy flirting with them, even though I love my partner deeply. I feel a wave of guilt and anxiety wash over me as I imagine myself succumbing to temptation and betraying my partner's trust. I try to push the thoughts away, but they linger in the back of my mind, whispering doubts about my commitment. As the day goes on, I find myself constantly checking in with my partner, seeking reassurance that everything is okay between us. I replay past conversations and interactions, searching for any sign that my feelings might be wavering. The intrusive thoughts continue to haunt me, suggesting that I am not as loyal as I believe myself to be. I feel trapped, unable to escape the cycle of doubt and fear that my OCD has created. I know that I must face these thoughts head-on, without giving in to the compulsions that only serve to fuel my anxiety. But the weight of the potential consequences is heavy, and I struggle to find the strength to resist the urge to seek reassurance once more.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts and fears that I may be secretly losing my mind and developing undiagnosed schizophrenia
Compulsion: Constantly analyzing my own thoughts and behaviors for signs of psychosis, asking others for reassurance about my sanity
Feared consequence: Having my mind irreversibly shattered by schizophrenia, becoming a permanent resident of a psychiatric ward
Script intensity: 5/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
It starts with a flicker of doubt, a momentary hesitation as I reach for my coffee mug. Did I already drink from it this morning, or was that just a delusion? The question hangs in my mind, casting shadows of uncertainty over everything I thought I knew. As the day wears on, the doubts multiply and grow, sprouting like weeds in the garden of my sanity. Every strange thought or unexplained sensation takes on a sinister new meaning. Is this what the onset of schizophrenia feels like? The blurring of lines between reality and fantasy, the erosion of my once-solid grip on the world? I try to push the fears away, but they come surging back with a vengeance. I catch myself staring at a blank wall for minutes on end, lost in a labyrinth of paranoid thoughts and fragmented memories. I can't remember the last time I had a rational, coherent train of thought. I'm terrified that I'm losing my mind, that my psyche is crumbling like a sandcastle in the tide. I look in the mirror and don't recognize the gaunt, haunted face staring back at me. Is that really me, or just a figment of my splintering imagination? I want to reach out for help, but I'm paralyzed by the fear that no one will believe me, that they'll just think I'm crazy. And maybe they're right. Maybe I am crazy, and this is all just a delusion. The thought sends me spiraling further into despair. I curl up in bed, hugging my knees to my chest, and wonder how long it will be before they come to take me away to the psychiatric ward where I'll spend the rest of my days in a haze of medications and madness. I don't know what's real anymore, and I'm not sure I ever will again.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts that I am secretly a pedophile and will act on it.
Compulsion: Checking news for stories about myself, avoiding children, mental checking if I'm aroused around kids.
Feared consequence: I will molest a child, be caught and punished, and burn in hell for my unforgivable sins.
Script intensity: 10/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I'm walking through the park and see a group of young children playing. My mind instantly fills with horrifying images of me molesting them. I try to push the thoughts away but they only get more vivid and graphic. I can almost feel their small bodies against me as I commit the most heinous acts. Bile rises in my throat but I don't look away. I deserve to feel the crushing guilt and shame of my own depraved mind. What if these thoughts are really my true desires? What if I'm just rationalizing my evil urges? I imagine the police breaking down my door, arresting me, and dragging me away as the children point and scream. The disgust and hatred in their eyes burns me. I'm led away in handcuffs, my face plastered on the news as a monster. In court, the judge condemns me to life in prison. I'm thrown in a cell, alone with my shame and self-loathing. I replay the abuse over and over, reveling in the graphic details. I know God has turned his back on me forever. I've damned myself to an eternity in hell, where I will be endlessly tortured for my unforgivable sins. I'm the scum of the earth, a predator who preys on the innocent. There is no redemption for me. I am pure evil, and I welcome the unending suffering I deserve for the rest of time.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts that I may be secretly a psychopath or sociopath despite appearing normal on the surface
Compulsion: Constantly analyzing my own behaviors and motivations, seeking reassurance from loved ones that I'm not a monster, avoiding certain people or situations
Feared consequence: Discovering that I am a psychopath and have been unknowingly harming others, losing my identity and humanity
Script intensity: 6/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I'm sitting at my desk at work, going through the motions of my job, when a thought suddenly strikes me with terrifying clarity: what if I'm a psychopath? What if everything I've ever done, every relationship I've built, has been a lie, a mask covering up the truth of who I really am? I try to push the thought away, but it lingers, growing stronger with every passing moment. I start to analyze every interaction I've ever had, looking for signs that I'm not quite human, that I lack the empathy and morality that define us as decent people. And the more I look, the more I start to find. The times I've manipulated people to get what I want. The way I can sometimes detach from my emotions, viewing the world with a cold, calculating eye. The secret, shameful fantasies of power and control that sometimes flash through my mind unbidden. Are these the signs of a psychopathic mind, waiting to emerge fully and wreak havoc on the world? I glance up and see my coworker, Sarah, walking by my office. She smiles at me, but I can't smile back. Because I suddenly realize that I don't really know how I feel about her, or anyone else. I know I should care about them, but when I search inside myself for that feeling, I come up empty. Just a void, a chilling lack of connection. And then the horrifying possibility hits me: what if this emptiness, this lack of empathy, is who I really am? What if I'm not a good person at all, but a monster in waiting, a ticking time bomb of violence and cruelty? I stand up abruptly, knocking over my chair. I have to get out of here, away from people, before I do something terrible. But even as I flee, I can't escape the awful truth: I may never know for sure if I'm a psychopath. And if I am, it's only a matter of time before my mask slips and the world sees me for the monster I really am. My life as I know it, my identity, my humanity - it's all a fragile illusion, ready to shatter at any moment and leave me lost in an endless void of moral darkness.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts that I may have hit a child while driving, without noticing.
Compulsion: Driving back to retrace my route and search the area for any signs of an accident or injured child.
Feared consequence: I will accidentally kill a child, be convicted of vehicular manslaughter, and spend life in prison as a hated child-killer.
Script intensity: 10/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
As I'm driving down the road, I feel a small bump. It's subtle, but it's definitely there. My heart starts racing as I realize that I may have just hit a child. I try to convince myself that it was just a pothole or a piece of debris, but the doubt lingers. I know I should turn around and check, but I'm too afraid of what I might find. I keep driving, my hands shaking on the wheel. The guilt and horror consume me as I imagine a child lying broken and alone on the side of the road, slowly dying because I was too much of a coward to stop and help. I picture the police showing up at my door, arresting me for hit-and-run and vehicular manslaughter. I'm dragged away in handcuffs as my family watches in disgust, realizing that I'm a child-killer. In court, the child's parents sob as they describe the loss of their precious child, all because of my negligence. I'm convicted and sent to prison for life, where I'm shunned and attacked by other inmates who know what I've done. Every day is a waking nightmare as I'm forced to confront the reality of what I've taken from the world. But I know that if I turn around and check, and there's nothing there, my OCD will never let me drive in peace again. So I have to keep going, leaving a child to die alone and face the consequences of my actions, all because of my intrusive thoughts and compulsions.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusively questioning core tenets of my faith and doubting the existence of God.
Compulsion: Excessively seeking reassurance from religious texts, clergy, and loved ones; avoiding any media or discussions that may challenge my beliefs.
Feared consequence: Abandoning my faith and facing eternal damnation for apostasy.
Script intensity: 4/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
As I sit in church, I can't help but question the very foundation of my beliefs. What if the Bible is just a book written by man, and not the infallible word of God? What if Jesus was just a prophet, and not the Son of God? These thoughts swirl in my head, making me feel sick to my stomach. I try to push them away, but they keep coming back, louder and more persistent each time. I look around at my fellow parishioners, wondering if they ever doubt their faith like I do. I feel like a fraud, sitting here and pretending to be a devout Christian when I have these intrusive thoughts. I want to stand up and shout, 'I don't know if I believe anymore!' But I'm too afraid of the consequences. What will my family think of me? What will my friends say? Will I be shunned by my community for questioning my faith? The thought of losing everything I hold dear terrifies me, but I can't shake these doubts. I don't know what to do. I can't talk to my priest about this; he would surely condemn me for my lack of faith. I'm stuck, trapped in a cycle of doubt and fear, with no way out. I feel like I'm on the brink of losing my faith entirely, and the thought of facing an uncertain eternity without God fills me with a deep, unending dread.

INPUT:
Obsession: Accidentally touching a contaminated surface and spreading E. coli bacteria to my infant daughter.
Compulsion: Repeatedly washing hands and surfaces with disinfectant; avoiding public spaces.
Feared consequence: My baby daughter contracts a life-threatening E. coli infection due to my negligence.
Script intensity: 4/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I imagine I'm out running errands with my infant daughter. We stop by the grocery store, and I place her carrier on top of the shopping cart. As I push the cart through the store, my mind begins to race with thoughts of all the germs and bacteria that could be lingering on the handle. I can't shake the image of E. coli bacteria transferring from the cart to my hands, and then to my daughter's mouth as I lift her out of the carrier. The anxiety builds as I continue shopping, knowing that I should wash my hands but feeling trapped in the store with no way to properly disinfect. As we leave the store, I can't help but notice the door handles, the ATM keypad, the pen at the signing desk - all potential sources of contamination. By the time we get home, my hands feel dirty and dangerous, as if they're covered in a layer of invisible bacteria just waiting to make my daughter sick. I want to scrub them raw, to use the strongest disinfectant I can find to eradicate any trace of E. coli. But I know I can't give in to the compulsion, so I resist. Instead, I try to distract myself as I prepare dinner, but the thoughts of contamination continue to plague me. What if I accidentally touched my daughter's face, her bottle, her toys? What if I've already spread the bacteria to every surface in our home? As the evening wears on, I watch my daughter closely, looking for any sign of illness. She seems healthy, thank goodness, but the uncertainty is torture. I know I'll spend the night tossing and turning, replaying every moment of our outing and second-guessing every decision. The fear that I may have unknowingly exposed my daughter to a life-threatening infection is a heavy burden to bear, and one that I will have to learn to live with in the face of this unrelenting OCD.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts that I may have unknowingly hit a child while driving, without feeling any impact.
Compulsion: Compulsively checking my rearview mirror for any sign of an accident, and mentally replaying my drive in excruciating detail.
Feared consequence: I will accidentally kill an innocent child, be convicted of vehicular manslaughter, and spend the rest of my life in prison as an unrepentant murderer.
Script intensity: 10/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
As I drive down the street, I feel a sudden jolt of terror as the thought strikes me - what if I just hit a child without even realizing it? My mind races, desperately trying to recall any unusual bumps or noises, but I can't be certain. The doubt gnaws at me, growing stronger with each passing second. I know I should keep driving, but the urge to turn around and check is overwhelming. What if there's a broken little body lying in the road, its life bleeding away while I do nothing? The guilt would be unbearable. But if I do check and find something, my life as I know it will be over. I'll be arrested, tried, and convicted of killing a child. I'll spend the rest of my days in a prison cell, hated by everyone as the monster who took an innocent life. Every day will be a living hell, haunted by the memory of what I've done and the knowledge that I deserve every moment of my punishment. But I have no choice. I have to take the risk of leaving a child to die alone and in agony, or face the very real possibility of losing my freedom, my reputation, and my sanity. The only way out is to confront my worst fear head-on and accept that I may have to live with the consequences of my actions, whatever they may be.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts that my sense of identity and reality may be an illusion, suspecting I may be a character in a simulation or video game
Compulsion: Checking behaviors to verify my own existence, like pinching myself or looking for glitches in my environment that would indicate a simulated reality
Feared consequence: The realization that my life, memories and identity are fabricated and that I am not a real person with genuine experiences and relationships
Script intensity: 3/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
As I go about my daily routine, a nagging doubt creeps into my thoughts. What if this isn't real? What if I'm not really here, living this life? The possibility that I may be nothing more than a character in a simulated world, or worse, a video game character, starts to consume me. I look at my hands, turning them over and examining them closely. They look real, but are they? I pinch my arm, feeling the pain, but is that just part of the programming? I walk down the street, watching the people pass by, and wonder if they are real or just NPCs, non-player characters designed to populate my fabricated world. The more I think about it, the more everything around me starts to feel fake, like a movie set. I start looking for glitches, for signs that this reality isn't as solid as it seems. I stare at a wall, waiting for the pixels to distort or the texture to repeat. I listen for audio loops in the background noise. I question everyone I talk to, searching for inconsistencies in their stories that would reveal them as artificial constructs. The uncertainty gnaws at me, eroding my sense of self. Who am I, really? Are my memories even mine, or were they programmed into me? Do my relationships, my accomplishments, my struggles, mean anything if they are just part of a simulation? The more I question, the more my identity seems to unravel, until I'm left with nothing but doubt and a gnawing sense of emptiness. I feel like I'm losing my grip on who I am, on what is real. And I don't know how to get it back.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts and mental images of myself committing heinous sins and acts of blasphemy.
Compulsion: Mental checking and confessing to priests or religious leaders to ensure I am still in God's grace.
Feared consequence: Eternal damnation and separation from God for my unforgivable sins and impure thoughts.
Script intensity: 3/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
As I kneel in prayer, unwanted images flood my mind. I see myself standing before an altar, defiling it with profane acts. The intrusive thoughts whisper that I am a fraud, unworthy of God's love. I try to push them away, but they linger, taunting me. Did I really mean my last confession, or was it just another empty ritual? The uncertainty gnaws at me, filling me with dread. What if these thoughts are a sign of my true nature, a sinful wretch destined for hell? I imagine the disappointed faces of my religious mentors as they learn the depths of my hidden depravity. The guilt is suffocating, but I resist the urge to seek reassurance. I must sit with this anxiety, even if it means questioning my faith. Perhaps I am already lost, doomed to an eternity separated from God. But I will not give in to the compulsions that have ruled my life. I will hold onto these disturbing thoughts, accepting the possibility of damnation, in order to break free from the chains of scrupulosity. Only time will tell if I have the strength to face my darkest fears without turning back to my rituals.

INPUT:
Obsession: I touched a public door handle covered in invisible feces and didn't wash properly.
Compulsion: Excessive handwashing in scalding water with bleach; mentally reviewing every object touched.
Feared consequence: Spreading deadly bacteria to family, watching them suffer and die, and being consumed by guilt and regret.
Script intensity: 10/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I reach out to open the heavy glass door to the grocery store, not thinking to avoid the handle. As my hand grips the metal, I imagine the thousands of people who have touched it before me, many of them not washing their hands after using the restroom. I picture tiny particles of feces, invisible to the naked eye, smeared on the surface from unwashed hands. My heart races as I realize I've just contaminated myself with their filth. I fight the urge to rush to the restroom to scrub my hands raw with scalding water and bleach. Instead, I continue shopping, the anxiety building with each item I touch. What if I'm spreading that bacteria to every product I handle? What if an elderly person or young child touches one of those items and gets sick? The guilt would be unbearable. As I load the groceries into my car, I can't stop thinking about the germs now coating my hands. I want so desperately to go back and wash them, to scrub until the skin is red and raw. But I don't. I drive home, my mind consumed with images of the bacteria multiplying, spreading, waiting to infect anyone I come in contact with. When I walk in the door, my children run to greet me. I recoil, not wanting to touch them, but it's too late. I've already embraced them, planting the seeds of a deadly illness on their skin. Over the next few days, I watch in horror as my family falls ill, one by one. Fever, vomiting, diarrhea - the telltale signs of a virulent bacterial infection. I'm consumed with regret, knowing I could have prevented this if only I had washed my hands. As they suffer, I suffer too, tormented by the knowledge that I am responsible. The doctors can do nothing to save them. One by one, they slip away, their final breaths a testament to my negligence. In the end, I am left alone, consumed by grief and guilt, a living testament to the dangers of invisible bacteria. I have no one to blame but myself.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts that I may have hit a pedestrian or cyclist while driving without noticing.
Compulsion: Driving back to retrace my route and check for injured people or evidence of a collision.
Feared consequence: Causing a severe or fatal accident, being charged with a crime, losing my freedom and reputation.
Script intensity: 7/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
As I drive down the busy city street, my mind is filled with doubts and fears. What if I hit someone and didn't even realize it? I try to reassure myself that I would have felt the impact or heard a scream, but the uncertainty gnaws at me. My heart races as I imagine the devastating consequences. I picture a mangled body lying in the road, a cyclist pinned under my car, their life bleeding out while I drive away obliviously. The guilt and horror would be overwhelming. I would be consumed by the knowledge that I took an innocent life, that I left someone to die alone and in pain. The police would eventually identify me from traffic cameras or witness reports. I would be arrested, charged with vehicular manslaughter or even murder. My reputation would be destroyed, my career and relationships in ruins. I would have to face the victim's grieving family in court, see the anguish and hatred in their eyes. I might spend years behind bars, haunted by what I've done, a pariah to society. And yet, I know that to overcome this OCD, I must resist the compulsion to check. I have to accept the risk, however remote, that I may have caused unspeakable harm and gotten away with it. I must continue driving, even as the intrusive thoughts torment me, even as I imagine the worst. It is a heavy burden to bear, but the only way to break free from the grip of my obsessions.

INPUT:
Obsession: Feeling an emotional connection with a male friend means I am secretly gay.
Compulsion: Analyzing the friendship and trying to prove to myself that I'm straight.
Feared consequence: Leaving my wife and destroying my life to pursue a relationship with a man.
Script intensity: 7/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I imagine myself hanging out with my close male friend. We've known each other for years and have a deep emotional bond. As we talk and laugh together, I start to wonder if there's something more to our connection. Could I be attracted to him? The thought sends chills down my spine. I try to push it away, but it keeps coming back. I analyze every interaction, every touch, every lingering glance. Is he feeling the same way? Do I want him to be? I feel a tightness in my chest as I imagine confessing my feelings to him. What if he reciprocates? What if we start a secret affair behind my wife's back? I picture us sneaking around, stolen moments of passion, the thrill of the forbidden. But then I think of my wife, my children. How could I do this to them? The guilt consumes me. I imagine having to sit them down and tell them that I'm leaving, that I've fallen in love with a man. The devastation on their faces, the shattered trust, the broken family. Is this what I want? But what if I don't act on it? What if I spend the rest of my life wondering, trapped in a loveless marriage, a mere shell of a man? The uncertainty is torture. I don't know what I want, who I am anymore. All I know is that these thoughts won't leave me alone. They haunt me day and night, eroding my sanity bit by bit. And so I continue on, caught between two impossible choices, praying for a resolution that may never come.

INPUT:
Obsession: I could sexually abuse my baby.
Compulsion: Avoiding being alone with the baby; showering the baby with affection to 'prove' I'm a good mother; mentally reviewing past interactions with the baby for signs of abuse.
Feared consequence: Actually sexually abusing my baby; being arrested and charged with child molestation; having my baby taken away by Child Protective Services; being shunned by family and friends.
Script intensity: 9/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I'm changing my baby daughter's diaper when a horrible thought pops into my head: 'What if I sexually abused her?' The thought is so disgusting and repulsive that I recoil in horror. But my OCD latches onto it, bombarding me with images of me molesting my own child. I feel physically ill, like I might throw up. I hurry to finish changing her diaper, hands shaking, and put her down as quickly as possible. I can't bear to be alone with her anymore. What if I act on these thoughts? What if I'm a monster disguised as a mother? I find myself constantly reviewing our past interactions, searching for any sign that I've already abused her. Did I change her diaper too slowly that one time? Did I linger too long on certain parts of her body? The doubts plague me endlessly. I try to shower her with extra affection, hugging her tightly and telling her how much I love her, as if that could somehow 'prove' I'm not a predator. But deep down, I'm terrified that I am. I imagine the police showing up at my door, arresting me for child molestation. I picture my baby being ripped from my arms by Child Protective Services, her tearful face accusing me of the worst betrayal. I envision myself in a courtroom, facing a judge and jury who see me as nothing more than a sick, twisted pervert. I imagine the looks of disgust and horror on my family and friends' faces when they find out what I've done. I'm shunned and ostracized, a pariah in my own community. And through it all, the unrelenting guilt and self-loathing, knowing that I've caused irreparable harm to my own innocent child. These thoughts and images haunt me constantly, a waking nightmare from which I can't escape. But I know I must face them head-on, no matter how excruciating it is. I can't let OCD rob me of my ability to be a loving, nurturing mother to my baby girl. So I confront the fear, day after day, knowing that each exposure, each moment of uncertainty, is a step towards reclaiming my life from this debilitating disorder.

INPUT:
Obsession: Intrusive thoughts that I may be secretly developing schizophrenia without realizing it
Compulsion: Avoiding situations that trigger my fear of schizophrenia, seeking excessive reassurance from mental health professionals, constantly monitoring my thoughts and perceptions for signs of psychosis
Feared consequence: Becoming permanently psychotic and losing my ability to function in society, ending up institutionalized or homeless
Script intensity: 5/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I'm walking down the street when I start to feel it - that familiar sense of detachment, like I'm not fully present in my own body. The world around me seems to warp and shift, colors bleeding into each other, the outlines of buildings and trees blurring at the edges. I try to focus on my breathing, on the sensation of my feet hitting the pavement, but it's like I'm experiencing everything through a thick fog. Voices start to whisper in my head, not quite loud enough for me to make out what they're saying. But I know they're there, and I know they're not supposed to be. Panic starts to set in as I realize I can't trust my own senses anymore. What if this is the beginning of the end? What if this is the moment my mind finally snaps, the moment I start my inevitable descent into full-blown schizophrenia? I can feel the terror rising in my throat, choking me. I look around desperately, searching for something, anything that can anchor me back to reality. But everything is strange and unfamiliar, like I'm seeing it all for the first time. The whispers in my head grow louder, more insistent. They're telling me things, horrible things, but I can't make sense of the words. All I know is that they fill me with a deep, primal dread. I start to run, my heart pounding in my chest, my lungs burning. I don't know where I'm going, but I know I have to get away. Away from the voices, away from the fear, away from the looming specter of madness that's been haunting me for months. But no matter how fast I run, I can't escape it. Because the true horror isn't out there somewhere, waiting to get me. It's already inside my head, gnawing away at my sanity, piece by piece. And there's nothing I can do to stop it.

INPUT:
Obsession: I could smother my baby while breastfeeding.
Compulsion: Pulling away from the baby; checking to see if the baby is breathing; avoiding breastfeeding.
Feared consequence: Accidentally smothering my baby; being an unfit mother; losing custody of my child.
Script intensity: 3/10
Exposure type: imaginal

OUTPUT:
I sit down in the rocking chair, cradling my newborn daughter in my arms as I prepare to breastfeed her. As I guide her towards my breast, the intrusive thought hits me: what if I smother her? I try to brush it off, but the doubt gnaws at me. What if I'm not holding her at the right angle? What if I accidentally cover her nose and mouth? I feel my heart rate quicken as I imagine her struggling to breathe, her tiny face turning blue. I pull her away from my breast, checking to see if she's okay. She looks up at me, her eyes wide and innocent, and I feel a wave of guilt wash over me. How could I even think such a thing? I must be a terrible mother. I try to continue breastfeeding, but the thoughts keep coming. What if I lose control and purposely smother her? What if I'm not fit to be a mother? I find myself avoiding breastfeeding, pumping and bottle-feeding instead, just to avoid the overwhelming anxiety. I know I need to face these fears head-on, but it's so hard when the stakes feel so high. What if I accidentally hurt my precious baby girl? The uncertainty eats away at me, leaving me exhausted and on edge. I love my daughter more than anything in the world, but these thoughts make me question my ability to care for her. I know I need to be strong, to push through the fear and doubt, but it's easier said than done.
